question:
For any function \(f:X\to Y\) and any subset \(A\) of \(Y\), define \(f^{-1}(A)=\{x\in X:f(x)\in A\}\). Let \(A^c\) denote the complement of \(A\) in \(Y\). For subsets \(A_1,A_2\) of \(Y\), consider the following statements:
\[
\text{(i)}\quad f^{-1}(A_1^c\cap A_2^c)=(f^{-1}(A_1))^c\cup(f^{-1}(A_2))^c
\]
\[
\text{(ii)}\quad \text{If }f^{-1}(A_1)=f^{-1}(A_2)\text{ then }A_1=A_2.
\]
Then,

options.B: (i) is always true, but (ii) may not always be true
options.C: (ii) is always true, but (i) may not always be true
